title: Interior latria vs dulia: supreme will-prostration to God as first principle and last end, vs lesser creaturely inclination
source_text: XI. Porro Latriam, id est, cultum Deo proprium a Dulia, id est, cultu creaturis debito docent facile & optime distingui quoad actus interiores. Nam latria interior est quaedam summa voluntatis prostratio, & inclinatio, cum apprehensione Dei ut primi principii, & ultimi finis, atque adeo summi boni, qualis adoratio soli Deo convenit. Dulia vero interior ipsis est longe minor inclinatio voluntatis, cum apprehensione alicujus excellentiae plusquam humanae quidem, sed multum infra divinam.
pass_a_gloss: Further they teach that Latria, that is, the cult proper to God, is easily and optimally distinguished from Dulia, that is, the cult owed to creatures, as regards interior acts. For interior latria is a certain supreme prostration and inclination of the will, with apprehension of God as first principle, and last end, and so of the supreme good, which adoration befits God alone. But interior dulia for them is a far lesser inclination of the will, with apprehension of some excellence indeed more than human, but much below the divine.
pass_b_english: Interiorly latria and dulia part cleanly.
Latria is the will’s highest prostration to God as first principle, last end, and supreme good.
Dulia is a lesser bow to more-than-human yet still creaturely excellence.

lemmas.gloss: of the first principle and last end

choices.why: God as ultimate object of latria’s interior act.
